([[Bell Buckle, Tennessee]]) | college = [[Tennessee Volunteers basketball|Tennessee]] (2020–2021) | draft_year = 2021 | draft_round = 1 | draft_pick = 21 | draft_team = [[New York Knicks]] | career_start = 2021 | years1 = {{nbay|2021|full=y}} | team1 = [[Los Angeles Clippers]] | years2 = [[2021–22 NBA G League season|2021–2022]] | team2 = →[[Agua Caliente Clippers]] | years3 = {{nbay|2021|end}}–{{nbay|2022|end}} | team3 = [[Portland Trail Blazers]] | years4 = {{nbay|2023|start}}–{{nbay|2024|end}} | team4 = [[Brooklyn Nets]] | years5 = [[2023–24 NBA G League season|2023–2024]] | team5 = →[[Long Island Nets]] | years6 = [[2025–26 NBA G League season|2025–2026]] | team6 = [[Maine Celtics]] | years7 = [[2026–27 NBA G League season|2026]]–present | team7 = [[College Park Skyhawks]] | highlights = * [[Southeastern Conference|SEC]] All-Freshman Team (2021) * 2× [[Tennessee Mr. Basketball]] (2018, 2019) }} '''Christopher Keon Johnson''' (born March 10, 2002) is an American professional [[basketball]] player for the [[College Park Skyhawks]] of the [[NBA G League]]. He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Tennessee Volunteers basketball|Tennessee Volunteers]]. Johnson was selected in the [[2021 NBA draft]] with the 21st overall pick by the [[New York Knicks]], but was traded to the [[Los Angeles Clippers]] on draft night. During his rookie season, the Clippers traded him to the [[Portland Trail Blazers]] with whom he played for until the end of the [[2022–23 NBA season|2022-23 season]]. After getting traded to and waived by the [[Phoenix Suns]] during the 2023 offseason, Johnson signed with the [[Brooklyn Nets]] with whom he had a breakout year during the [[2024–25 NBA season|2024-25 season]]. ==Early life== Two months before beginning high school, Johnson suffered [[open fracture]]s in four of his fingers, was thrown about 10 feet and lost consciousness in a [[fireworks]] accident. He underwent surgery to repair [[blood vessel]]s in his hand and avoid [[amputation]], and he underwent eight weeks of intensive [[physical therapy]].{{Cite web |last=Humphrey |first=Nancy |date=June 10, 2019 |title=Game On |url=https://hope.childrenshospitalvanderbilt.org/game-on/ |access-date=May 5, 2020 |publisher=Vanderbilt Children's Hospital}}{{Cite web |last=Kreager |first=Tom |date=February 13, 2019 |title=How top prospect Keon Johnson, wanted by UT Vols and others, almost ended his career before it began |url=https://www.tennessean.com/story/sports/high-school/2019/02/13/nashville-high-school-basketball-ut-vols-keon-johnson-webb-school/2805130002/ |access-date=May 5, 2020 |website=[[The Tennessean]]}} Johnson played high school basketball for [[The Webb School (Bell Buckle, Tennessee)|The Webb School]] in [[Bell Buckle, Tennessee]]. In his sophomore season, he averaged 25.6 points, 10.2 rebounds, and 4.1 assists per game, earning Division II-A [[Tennessee Mr. Basketball]] honors.{{Cite web |date=April 16, 2018 |title=2017–18 ALL-USA Tennessee Boys Basketball Team |url=https://usatodayhss.com/2018/2017-18-all-usa-tennessee-boys-basketball-team |access-date=May 5, 2020 |publisher=USA Today High School Sports}} As a junior, Johnson averaged 25.3 points, 9.4 rebounds and 3.7 assists per game, leading his team to the Division II-A state semifinals. He repeated as Division II-A Tennessee Mr. Basketball.{{Cite web |last=Kreager |first=Tom |date=March 1, 2019 |title=Keon Johnson, Tennessee's top 2020 basketball prospect, plays with edge, even if that means technicals |url=https://www.tennessean.com/story/sports/high-school/2019/03/01/tennessee-high-school-basketball-webb-star-keon-johnson-fouls-out-state-tssaa/3036815002/ |access-date=May 5, 2020 |website=[[The Tennessean]]}}{{Cite web |last=Kreager |first=Tom |date=March 5, 2019 |title=James Wiseman, top college basketball prospect in country, wins first Mr. Basketball honor |url=https://www.tennessean.com/story/sports/high-school/2019/03/05/tssaa-mr-and-miss-basketball-winners-announced/3052881002/ |access-date=March 5, 2020 |website=[[The Tennessean]]}} Early in his senior season, Johnson suffered a season-ending [[Meniscus (anatomy)|meniscus]] injury. In four games, he averaged 30.5 points with 10.5 rebounds and 5.8 assists per game.{{Cite web |last=Kreager |first=Tom |date=December 17, 2019 |title=Tennessee basketball signee Keon Johnson injures knee, expected back before postseason |url=https://www.tennessean.com/story/sports/high-school/2019/12/17/tennessee-basketball-keon-johnson-injures-knee-out-six-weeks/2677356001/ |access-date=March 5, 2020 |website=[[The Tennessean]]}} On August 6, 2019, Johnson committed to play [[college basketball]] for [[Tennessee Volunteers basketball|Tennessee]] over offers from [[Ohio State Buckeyes men's basketball|Ohio State]] and [[Virginia Cavaliers men's basketball|Virginia]], among others.{{Cite web |date=August 6, 2019 |title=Big in-state recruit Keon Johnson commits to Tennessee |url=https://www.wvlt.tv/content/news/Big-In-State-recruit-picks-Tennessee-524260141.html |access-date=May 5, 2020 |publisher=[[WVLT-TV]]}} By the end of his high school career, Johnson was rated by major recruiting services as a consensus five-star [[college recruiting|recruit]] and the highest ranked player in Tennessee in the 2020 class. He became the first top-ranked in-state prospect to commit to Tennessee since [[Robert Hubbs III]] in 2013.{{Cite web |last=Wilson |first=Mike |date=November 13, 2019 |title=Tennessee basketball signs three prominent recruits Wednesday |url=https://www.knoxnews.com/story/sports/college/university-of-tennessee/mens-basketball/2019/11/13/tennessee-vols-basketball-recruiting-jaden-springer-keon-johnson-rick-barnes/2556897001/ |access-date=May 5, 2020 |website=[[Knoxville News Sentinel]]}} {{College Athlete Recruit Start|40=no|collapse=no|year=2020}} {{College Athlete Recruit Entry | recruit = Keon Johnson | position = [[Shooting guard|SG]] | hometown = [[Shelbyville, Tennessee|Shelbyville, TN]] | highschool = [[The Webb School (Bell Buckle, Tennessee)|The Webb School]] (TN) | feet = 6 | inches = 5 | weight = 180 | 40 = | commitdate = August 9, 2019 | scout stars = | rivals stars = 5 | 247 stars = 5 | espn stars = 5 | espn grade = 90 }} {{College Athlete Recruit End | 40 = | year = 2020 | rivals ref title = Tennessee 2020 Basketball Commitments | scout ref title = | espn ref title = 2020 Tennessee Volunteers Recruiting Class | rivals school = tennessee | scout s = | espn schoolid = 2633 | 247 overall = 17 | rivals overall = 18 | espn overall = 28 | access-date = August 18, 2020 | bball = yes }} ==College career== On February 6, 2021, Johnson scored a career-high 27 points in an 82–71 win over [[Kentucky Wildcats men's basketball|Kentucky]].{{Cite web |date=February 6, 2021 |title=Johnson, Springer rally No. 11 Tennessee past Kentucky 82–71 |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=401258790 |access-date=July 21, 2021 |website=[[ESPN]] |publisher=[[Associated Press]]}} As a freshman, he averaged 11.3 points, 3.5 rebounds and 2.5 assists per game, and was named to the [[Southeastern Conference]] (SEC) All-Freshman Team. On April 7, 2021, Johnson declared for the [[2021 NBA draft]], forgoing his college eligibility.{{Cite web |last=Givony |first=Jonathan |date=April 7, 2021 |title=Tennessee Vols' Keon Johnson to declare for NBA draft |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/31209073/tennessee-vols-keon-johnson-declare-nba-draft |access-date=July 21, 2021 |website=[[ESPN]]}} At the [[NBA Draft Combine]], he recorded the highest maximum [[vertical jump|vertical leap]] in combine history, at 48 inches.{{Cite web |last=Taylor |first=Cody |date=June 24, 2021 |title=Keon Johnson shatters combine record with historic max vertical jump |url=https://therookiewire.usatoday.com/2021/06/24/keon-johnson-nba-draft-combine-max-vertical-jump-record/ |access-date=July 21, 2021 |website=Rookie Wire}} ==Professional career== ===Los Angeles Clippers (2021–2022)=== Johnson was selected with the 21st pick in the [[2021 NBA draft]] by the [[New York Knicks]] and was traded to the [[Los Angeles Clippers]] for [[Quentin Grimes]] and draft considerations.{{Cite news |last=Wilson |first=Mike |date=July 29, 2021 |title=Tennessee basketball's Keon Johnson picked No. 21 by New York Knicks in 2021 NBA Draft |url=https://www.knoxnews.com/story/sports/college/university-of-tennessee/mens-basketball/2021/07/29/keon-johnson-nba-draft-new-york-knicks-los-angeles-clippers-tennessee-basketball/7987250002/ |access-date=July 30, 2021 |work=[[Knoxville News-Sentinel]]}} On August 6, 2021, he signed his rookie scale contract with the Clippers.{{Cite web |last=Adams |first=Luke |date=August 6, 2021 |title=Clippers Sign Keon Johnson To Rookie Contract |url=https://www.hoopsrumors.com/2021/08/clippers-sign-keon-johnson-to-rookie-contract.html |access-date=February 7, 2023 |website=Hoops Rumors}} In his rookie year, Johnson played in only 15 games for the Clippers.{{Cite web |title=Keon Johnson Stats, Height, Weight, Position, Draft Status and more |url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/j/johnske07.html |access-date=July 6, 2025 |website=Basketball-Reference.com |language=en}} ===Portland Trail Blazers (2022–2023)=== On February 4, 2022, Johnson was traded, alongside [[Eric Bledsoe]], [[Justise Winslow]], and a 2025 second-round pick, to the [[Portland Trail Blazers]] in exchange for [[Norman Powell]] and [[Robert Covington]].{{Cite web |date=February 4, 2022 |title=Trail Blazers Acquire Eric Bledsoe, Keon Johnson and Justise Winslow |url=https://www.nba.com/blazers/trail-blazers-acquire-eric-bledsoe-keon-johnson-and-justise-winslow |access-date=February 5, 2022 |website=NBA.com}} Johnson made his Trail Blazers debut on February 24, recording four points and four rebounds in a 132–95 loss to the [[Golden State Warriors]].{{Cite web |last=Peterson |first=Anne M. |date=February 25, 2022 |title=CURRY, WARRIORS RETURN FROM ALL-STAR BREAK TO ROUT BLAZERS |url=https://www.nba.com/game/0022100894 |access-date=March 15, 2023 |website=NBA.com}} On April 1, he scored a career-high 20 points, alongside three assists, in a 130–111 loss to the [[San Antonio Spurs]].{{Cite web |last=Dominguez |first=Raul |date=April 1, 2022 |title=SPURS MAINTAIN 10TH PLACE IN WEST WITH BIG WIN OVER BLAZERS |url=https://www.nba.com/game/0022101158 |access-date=March 15, 2023 |website=NBA.com}} The Trail Blazers ultimately finished the season with a 27–55 record and did not qualify for the playoffs for the first time since [[2013 NBA playoffs|2013]]. Johnson played for the Trail Blazers during the [[2022 NBA Summer League]]. He averaged 14.2 points per game en route to the team's second Las Vegas Summer League championship in franchise history.{{Cite web |last=Fentress |first=Aaron |date=July 21, 2022 |title=Portland Trail Blazers summer league review |url=https://www.oregonlive.com/blazers/2022/07/portland-trail-blazers-summer-league-review.html |access-date=March 15, 2023 |website=The Oregonian}} On March 27, 2023, he tied his career high of 20 points, alongside three rebounds and six assists, in a 124–90 loss to the [[New Orleans Pelicans]].{{Cite web |last=Peterson |first=Anne M. |date=March 28, 2023 |title=INGRAM SCORES 29 AS PELICANS ROUT TRAIL BLAZERS 124–90 |url=https://www.nba.com/game/0022201127 |access-date=April 1, 2023 |website=NBA.com}} Two days later, Trail Blazers head coach [[Chauncey Billups]] announced that Johnson had suffered a broken finger during a practice and would be out indefinitely.{{Cite web |date=March 29, 2023 |title=Trail Blazers' Keon Johnson: Suffers broken finger |url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/trail-blazers-keon-johnson-suffers-broken-finger/ |access-date=March 31, 2023 |website=CBSSports.com}} On September 27, 2023, Johnson, alongside [[Grayson Allen]], [[Jusuf Nurkić]], and [[Nassir Little]] was traded to the [[Phoenix Suns]] as part of a three-team trade that sent [[Damian Lillard]] to the [[Milwaukee Bucks]] and [[Jrue Holiday]], [[Toumani Camara]], [[Deandre Ayton]], and a 2029 first-round draft pick to the Portland Trail Blazers.{{Cite web |date=September 27, 2023 |title=SUNS ACQUIRE NURKIĆ, ALLEN, LITTLE, JOHNSON |url=https://www.nba.com/suns/news/suns-acquire-nurkic-allen-little-johnson |access-date=September 27, 2023 |website=NBA.com}} The Suns later waived him on October 23 ahead of the 2023–24 regular season roster cut deadline.{{Cite web |date=October 23, 2023 |title=Suns waive Keon Johnson, Bol Bol makes opening night roster |url=https://arizonasports.com/story/3536518/keon-johnson-cut-bol-bol-makes-suns-roster/ |access-date=October 24, 2023 |website=ArizonaSports.com}} ===Brooklyn Nets (2023–2025)=== On November 1, 2023, Johnson signed a [[two-way contract]] with the [[Brooklyn Nets]].{{Cite web |date=November 1, 2023 |title=Brooklyn Nets Sign Keon Johnson to Two-Way Contract |url=https://www.nba.com/nets/news/brooklyn-nets-sign-keon-johnson-to-two-way-contract |access-date=November 5, 2023 |website=NBA.com}} On July 21, 2024, Johnson re-signed with the Nets on a multi-year deal.{{Cite web |date=July 21, 2024 |title=Brooklyn Nets Sign Keon Johnson |url=https://www.nba.com/nets/news/brooklyn-nets-sign-keon-johnson |access-date=July 21, 2024 |website=NBA.com}} On September 17, 2025, the Nets waived Johnson, making him a free agent.{{Cite web |last=Fox |first=Kyler |date=September 17, 2025 |title=How Keon Johnson Will Be Remembered in Brooklyn |url=https://www.si.com/nba/nets/news/how-keon-johnson-will-be-remembered-in-brooklyn |access-date=September 17, 2025 |website=[[Sports Illustrated]]}} === Maine Celtics (2025–2026) === On December 1, 2025, Johnson signed with the [[Maine Celtics]] of the [[NBA G League]].{{Cite web |date=December 1, 2025 |title=Maine Celtics add NBA veteran Keon Johnson
